The battery chemistry is probably one of those new fancy chemistry anodes. the anode in a lithium battery is the primary point of failure, build up of dendrites on the anode increase the cells resistance generating heat increasing the discharge rate that then damages the batteries internal structure. There is a new to the market lithium iron phosphate technology that's turning up in phones and laptops which can offer 20-30% power (as in drive something bigger without blowing up meaning you can pack more folds into a single cell and increase mAh capacity) and a pretty substantial charge cycle increase. Lithium oxygen, lithium sodium mixes are generating lot of noise for the same reasons but they are a few years off yet.
